note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world (how many courts a park has, where it is, when the park is open) come from Louisville Parks and Recreation and the US Census geocoder and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Jefferson County. This is the first county in Kentucky this directory has published in, and it is an unusual one: Louisville and Jefferson County are a single consolidated government, with a handful of small cities inside it that stayed separately incorporated.

slots.coverage:
One city in Jefferson County is published here: Louisville, with sixteen venues and sixty-seven courts checked against the City's own pages.

Jefferson County is not an ordinary county for this purpose. Louisville and the county merged into one consolidated government, Louisville Metro, so the City of Louisville covers nearly all of the county. The Census geocoder names it two ways: "Louisville city" for addresses inside the pre-merger boundary and "Louisville/Jefferson County metro government (balance)" for the rest. Both are Louisville and both publish.

What the merger left behind is a set of small cities that stayed separately incorporated: Lyndon, Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Shively and others. Not one of those has been read against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site. Louisville Metro's own pickleball list includes a venue in one of them. Hounz Lane Park, with three courts at 2300 Hounz Ln., is run by the Metro parks department and placed by the Census in Lyndon city. It is refused from the Louisville page for that reason and named here rather than dropped.
slots.distribution:
What we cover is spread across sixteen parks rather than gathered into a complex, and the spread runs the whole length of the consolidated city. No two published venues share a postcode.

Charlie Vettiner Park's fourteen courts are the one large set, more than twice any other. Four parks hold six: Fern Creek, Hays Kennedy, Wyandotte and Nelson Hornbeck. Four hold four, Des Pres holds three, four hold two and two hold one. The parks themselves range from McNeely Lake's 746 acres and Iroquois's 725.85 to New Walnut Street's 5.74, and the courts are a single word on each park's amenity list, so at the large parks the address locates the park and not the courts.

Every one of the sixty-seven courts is outdoor on the City's word, and every park is open from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. on its own page, the same line at all sixteen. What the City does not publish is uniform too: no lighting, no price, no surface and no nets at any venue.
slots.gaps:
This is a Louisville page under a county heading, and in this county that is closer to the truth than usual, because the city is the county for most purposes.

The gap is the small cities. Lyndon, Jeffersontown, St. Matthews, Shively and the other separately incorporated cities inside Jefferson County have not been read, and nothing here says whether any of them publishes a court count of its own. Some may have no parks page to read, and their residents may play at Metro parks. That is what the Hounz Lane refusal illustrates: a court that exists, is counted by a municipal operator, and cannot publish, not for want of a fact but because of where the address falls.

Inside Louisville the gaps are of a different kind. Fern Creek and Riverview publish on the pickleball list alone, because their park pages do not mention the courts. The City says nothing about lighting, price, surface or nets anywhere, which means sixty-seven courts and not one answer to the questions people most often ask. Nothing outside the Metro parks department appears here: no club, no school, no commercial venue.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Nobody publishes an answer for the whole county. What has been checked is 67 courts across sixteen venues, all in Louisville, each with a source and a date you can see. Louisville Metro's own list names a seventeenth venue, Hounz Lane Park with three courts, that sits in Lyndon and is not published, and the county's other small cities have not been read.

faqs.q: Why is Hounz Lane Park not listed?
faqs.a: Louisville Metro runs it and lists it with three courts, but the Census geocoder places "2300 Hounz Ln." in Lyndon city, a separately incorporated small city inside Jefferson County. A city page holds venues in that city, and who runs them is a separate question.

faqs.q: Which venues here have lights, and which are free?
faqs.a: None that anyone can say. The City states no lighting and no price for any venue, so every Louisville court is recorded as not stated on both, and there is no lights page and no free page for the county. The only filter page is outdoor, which holds all sixteen venues.

sources.evidence: All sixteen published addresses matched at house-number level in Jefferson County, KY (FIPS 21111). Six were placed by the Census address file in "Louisville city" (Iroquois, Crescent Hill, George Rogers Clark, Wyandotte, Tyler, New Walnut Street) and seven in "Louisville/Jefferson County metro government (balance)" (McNeely Lake, Sun Valley, Des Pres, Fern Creek, Petersburg, Riverview, Riverside Gardens). Three resolved through OpenStreetMap in "Louisville": Charlie Vettiner and Nelson Hornbeck because the Census file holds no record of the address, Hays Kennedy because the Census answered "7003 BEECHLAND AVE, LOUISVILLE, KY, 40258" for "7003 Beachland Beach Rd." "2300 Hounz Ln." (Hounz Lane Park) is placed in "Lyndon city". The sixteen published postcodes are all different. Snapshot: data/sources/louisville-county-census.json
sources.not_stated: Anything about the courts themselves, or about any address in the other small cities.
